result.title: Task-Efficient Agent Evaluation Using Cached Traces
result.summary: Efficient benchmarking estimates a system's full benchmark performance from a small number of task executions. Standard approaches rely solely on the binary correctness of executions from a collection of already-evaluated reference systems. An agentic system, however, produces a rich trace for each execution that can reveal substantially more about its capabilities. Leveraging this information requires useful trace representations. We propose representing a trace by extracting a structured summary of it with an LLM and embedding the summary with a standard text encoder. These representations preserve correctness- and task-related signal while minimizing the presence of system identity-, model family- and harness-related signals that dominate raw trace embeddings. Given this representation for each task execution from all reference systems, we construct low-dimensional representations of the systems and predict a new system's score from its position among the reference systems. On SWE-bench Verified and Terminal-Bench 2.0, augmenting an item-response model with this geometry-based prediction reduces mean absolute error from 0.13 to 0.08 (Wilcoxon $p < 10^{-4}$) and from 0.14 to 0.12 (Wilcoxon $p < 10^{-3}$), respectively, when provided a single random executed task. Further, given access to the full set of reference systems, our approach dominates baselines for any given number of executed tasks on both benchmarks.

AI.brief_summary: 论文用 LLM 将 agent 执行轨迹抽成结构化摘要并文本嵌入，据此构建参考系统的低维几何表示，由少量已执行任务预测新系统在 SWE-bench Verified 与 Terminal-Bench 2.0 上的整体得分，以降低评测成本。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「保留任务与正确性信号、抑制模型身份与 harness 信号」的轨迹表示与去混杂思路，可供核查 latent 状态相似度中内容、系统与实现差异的分离及小样本评价设计。
